Hijri-based dates for 2027 are expected by the Umm al-Qura calendar and may shift by a day with moon sighting; each country announces its holidays by official decision. Government-sector holidays can differ in length from the private sector. For Ramadan and Eid dates see the Ramadan countdown.

Frequently asked questions

What is the next public holiday in the GCC?

In November and December 2026: Oman's National Day (holiday on 25–26 November), the UAE's Eid Al Etihad on 2–3 December, Bahrain's National Day on 16–17 December and Qatar's on 18 December. Then New Year's Day in the UAE, Kuwait and Bahrain, Saudi Founding Day on 22 February 2027, and Kuwait's National and Liberation Days on 25–26 February.

How many days off for Eid al-Fitr 2027 in the GCC?

For the private sector: 4 days in Saudi Arabia, 4 in Oman (possibly 5) starting on 8 March, 3 in the UAE (4 if Ramadan completes 30 days), and 3 in Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain. The first day of Eid is expected on Tuesday 9 March 2027 by the Umm al-Qura calendar.

Do workers get extra pay for working on a public holiday?

Yes in all six countries, at different rates: in the UAE a day's wage plus 50% of basic or a substitute day, in Saudi Arabia overtime pay or compensatory leave, and in Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman and Qatar at rates set out on each country's page.
